newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kinshasa opposition says 54 militants detained.
newsitem.headline: Kinshasa opposition says 54 militants detained.

text.p: A radical opposition party in President Laurent Kabila's Congo said on Monday that 54 of its activists were still in detention after breaking a ban on politics by joining a protest march.

A spokesman for the PALU party, which is loyal to the memory of slain nationalist independence leader Patrice Lumumba, told a news conference that one person was killed when troops opened fire during Friday's march and 133 were wounded.
"Up until now, the provisional death toll is one. Ten people have sustained bullet wounds and 123 have been injured in other ways," Godefroid Mayobo said. "Fifty four are still being detained."
Witnesses put Friday's toll at up to three. Interior Minister Mwenze Kongolo said no one had been killed.
Kabila, who toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May, said on Sunday that march organisers were to be held responsible for any casualty caused by the police.
Kabila, who says he too is a follower of Lumumba, has banned political activity and granted himself sweeping powers as president.
"How can those who claim to be Lumumbists resort to violence to put down peaceful demonstrations? Everybody knows that Lumumba himself was committed to non-violent means, so is PALU," Mayobo said.
PALU, he added, opposed Kabila's "democracy for the mute".
He said Kabila's soldiers had ransacked the home of PALU's veteran leader Antoine Gizenga.
